problem_checks.source: PDF p19 Remark3.9 and Lemma3.10; exact GR arXiv2210.02295v2 p2 Theorem1.1
problem_checks.independent_reasoning: The remark applies the conjugacy theorem to a C3 geodesic flow from a C4 metric and writes C3 conjugacy. The actual cited convention is C^(r*)=C^(r-1,Lip) at integer r, giving C^(2,Lip). This does not itself invalidate distribution pullback or the needed composition estimates: bounded weak third derivatives and the H2/H^(3/2) remainder traces leave room for a repair.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: A complete WF^2 covariance/propagation argument under the actual C^(2,Lip) map, with the finite-regularity tomography/Pestov interfaces, or a justified C3 upgrade is still missing. The smooth result is unaffected by this unresolved supplementary endpoint. The issue is not promoted to a confirmed error or a counterexample.

problem_checks.source: PDF pp8?18 and retained exact external interfaces
problem_checks.independent_reasoning: The time-preserving smooth conjugacy is obtained from equality of marked lengths in all nontrivial free homotopy classes and is homotopic to the natural bundle identification; arbitrary orbit equivalence is not substituted. It preserves contact form/volume. PSU Theorem5.6 provides a positive-Fourier invariant distribution with prescribed first mode under Anosov, without an extra negative-curvature assumption, with the required 2pi adjoint normalization. The two-sided maximal invariant wavefront set is the positive cone, strictly positive on V away from zero; this controls the Fourier pushforward and the negative Szego interface. The closed current f d(lambda), a wavefront-controlled Hodge primitive, and both noncharacteristic restrictions justify homology/Stokes pairing. Torelli gives unmarked conformal equivalence first. The finite-cover argument then handles the mapping-class ambiguity using ABMP TheoremC, including separating simple curves, and a uniform length ratio over all free homotopy classes, including nonsimple projections. Finally equal area and periodic-orbit approximation give int e^f >= area; Cauchy?Schwarz gives the reverse bound, forcing f=0.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: The local orientation correction gives T_tau=cos(theta)X-sin(theta)H and the matching oriented form. The integral int exp(ik theta)sin(theta)dtheta=i*pi(delta_k,1-delta_k,-1), with the 2pi normalization, recovers the actual downstream pairing 2i int f d(lambda)=-int pi_1*f. The preliminary sign slips therefore do not generate a new substantive problem. Full proofs of the external conjugacy, tomography and finite-cover theorems are not newly reproduced.
